record.title: On-policy distillation improves reported reasoning retention at sub-3-bit weights
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint studies why quantization-aware distillation can preserve short-form answers yet leave long mathematical and code generations impaired at sub-3-bit weight precision. The authors add on-policy distillation (OPD), which samples through the deployment quantized path and applies teacher guidance to the student's own generated prefixes, alongside task verifiers. Across Qwen3 and Falcon3 models at 2.79 and 1.88 effective weight bits, they report higher math and code benchmark performance than the QAD starting checkpoints, including gains over a matched-budget continued-QAD control in all 16 reported comparisons. The released QAOPD repository links checkpoints and reproduction instructions. These remain author-reported benchmark results; independent reproduction is open. The paper also reports a material implementation caveat: OPD uses a 16-bit KV cache in the principal arms rather than the released 8-bit KV-cache configuration, a deviation the authors say favors their results.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors published a preprint and linked a public QAOPD repository with evaluation checkpoints and instructions for evaluating released weights and reproducing OPD phase 1.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across four models at 2.79 and 1.88 effective weight bits, the authors report that OPD raises average BF16 performance retention on MATH-500 from 35% to 70% and on HumanEval from 66% to 91%, while preserving short-form performance.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that OPD outperforms continued teacher-forced QAD in all 16 matched-budget comparisons shown for GSM8K, MATH-500, MBPP and HumanEval, with shared starting checkpoints, corpora, phase schedules, step counts, learning rates and samples per step.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For selected configurations, the authors report OPD recovery using fewer GPU-hours than QAD initialization, including 57 versus 820 GPU-hours for Qwen3-4B at 1.88 bits and 11 versus 253 GPU-hours for Falcon3-1B-Instruct at 2.79 bits; these figures compare different stages and do not establish total-cost superiority over alternative deployment pipelines.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The principal OPD arms use a 16-bit KV cache, while the released EdgeRazor configuration referenced for comparison uses an 8-bit KV cache; the authors state this deviation favors their results.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper reports reproducing its QAD initialization from the released recipe, with a smaller effective batch than the recipe specifies and the optional offline regeneration step omitted; the reported QAD and OPD comparisons inherit these stated deviations.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of OPD results, matched-QAD control, or released-checkpoint evaluation has been completed.
The principal OPD results use a 16-bit KV cache rather than the referenced released 8-bit KV configuration; performance under a deployment-matched 8-bit KV cache is unknown.
Transfer beyond four small-to-mid-sized checkpoints and the selected math, code and short-form tasks has not been established.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported low-bit reasoning recovery holds under independent reproduction and deployment-matched KV-cache conditions, it could materially improve inference capability per weight-memory budget for some model families. Score 5 reflects the potential consequence within low-bit deployment, not confidence in the reported effect or broad transfer.
limitations: All performance and training-budget results are reported by the paper authors; this activation did not run the repository or reproduce any table.
The principal OPD experiments use a 16-bit KV cache rather than the released 8-bit configuration, so they do not directly demonstrate the same results with a fully 8-bit KV deployment path.

The paper's reproduced QAD starting point uses a smaller effective batch than the released recipe specifies and omits optional offline teacher regeneration; comparisons inherit those implementation choices.
The matched control and quantization baselines are author-run; independent baseline alignment, seed variation and hardware replication remain open.
Benchmark results cover four model checkpoints and fixed math, code and QA tasks; transfer to larger models, other architectures, other tasks and real serving workloads is not established.
GPU-hour comparisons are for selected training stages, not total pipeline cost, inference latency, energy, or a complete deployment cost model.

brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint studies why quantization-aware distillation can preserve short-form answers yet leave long mathematical and code generations impaired at sub-3-bit weight precision. The authors add on-policy distillation (OPD), which samples through the deployment quantized path and applies teacher guidance to the student's own generated prefixes, alongside task verifiers. Across Qwen3 and Falcon3 models at 2.79 and 1.88 effective weight bits, they report higher math and code benchmark performance than the QAD starting checkpoints, including gains over a matched-budget continued-QAD control in all 16 reported comparisons. The released QAOPD repository links checkpoints and reproduction instructions. These remain author-reported benchmark results; independent reproduction is open. The paper also reports a material implementation caveat: OPD uses a 16-bit KV cache in the principal arms rather than the released 8-bit KV-cache configuration, a deviation the authors say favors their results.

technical.claimed_result: At 2.79 and 1.88 effective weight bits, the authors report higher math and code results after OPD across Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B and Falcon3-1B-Instruct. They report average BF16 retention on MATH-500 rising from 35% to 70% and HumanEval from 66% to 91%; all 16 Table 4 matched-budget comparisons favor OPD over continued QAD. Gains vary materially by model and task.
technical.compute_or_cost: OPD-stage examples use 57 GPU-hours versus 820 for QAD initialization on Qwen3-4B W1.88, and 11 versus 253 on Falcon3-1B-Instruct W2.79. The comparison is between training stages; full pipeline cost and serving energy or latency are not established.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint, tables and author-linked public repository are directly inspectable. The reported benchmark outcomes and training-cost comparisons are CLAIMED by the authors, not independently reproduced in this activation.
technical.implementation_status: Authors report trained checkpoints and publish a repository with evaluation and OPD phase-1 reproduction instructions. No local execution or independent reproduction was done.
technical.mechanism: The student samples completions through its deployment quantized forward path. A frozen BF16 teacher supplies token-level feedback on prefixes from those sampled trajectories, while task verifiers score final-answer correctness in mathematics and test execution in code. The pipeline starts from QAD so that the low-bit policy remains viable before on-policy recovery.
technical.novelty: The paper applies on-policy teacher feedback to student trajectories generated under sub-3-bit deployment quantization, pairing dense token-level supervision with task verification to target errors that accumulate outside teacher-forced training prefixes.
technical.regime: Four model checkpoints (Qwen3-0.6B, 1.7B and 4B; Falcon3-1B-Instruct), 2.79 and 1.88 effective weight bits, INT8 activations and INT4 embeddings/output heads; math, code and short-form benchmark suites. Principal OPD arms use a 16-bit KV cache. This is an author-run preprint experiment, not a production-serving or broad model-family evaluation.
technical.reproducibility: The paper supplies detailed tables and an author-linked repository with checkpoints and instructions. Independent execution remains outstanding. The authors disclose a smaller effective batch and omitted optional offline regeneration in QAD reproduction; OPD uses KV16 rather than the released KV8 configuration, which they note favors their results.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper's strongest direct baseline is continued teacher-forced QAD from a shared QAD checkpoint under matched corpora, phase schedules, optimizer steps, learning rates and samples per step, evaluated on GSM8K, MATH-500, MBPP and HumanEval (Table 4). Its additional quantization-method comparison uses Qwen3-1.7B at aligned low-bit settings, but some methods use wider whole-bit fallbacks and generative benchmark head/embedding precision differs.

brief.title: On-policy distillation improves reported reasoning retention at sub-3-bit weights
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported gains reproduce, training on the trajectories a quantized model actually visits could recover some long-form reasoning and coding capability at very low weight precision, potentially improving the quality-cost frontier for constrained inference. The result is limited to four small-to-mid-sized model families/configurations and the paper's benchmark protocols; it does not establish a general low-bit solution or end-to-end deployment advantage.
